title: TypeScript insert axes preserve excess whitespace before the inserted token
symptom: Several TypeScript insert axes can report PASS while retaining an over-wide column because the axis interval starts at the inserted token, after pre-existing whitespace that should be available to the alignment calculation. In the `headers.ts` reproduction, `if` closing parentheses remain at column 18 although the longest condition requires column 15; the checker reports PASS with zero edits. Inspection also found the same boundary pattern in method-signature open/close parens and case-clause colons.

rootCause.summary: Several insert-axis boundaries started at the inserted token and excluded available pre-existing horizontal whitespace. Candidate v2 retains the bounded correction and regressions; final full check/self-use and the Opus fix-only review passed. The observed defect does not establish that every TypeScript insert axis or syntax form is covered.

requestedOutcome: For supported insert-axis forms, compute the shared token column from the actual preceding expression/name/label content and minimum required gap, removing excess existing whitespace without changing tokens, comments, or neighboring unsupported syntax.
decisions: Treat the issue as one shared boundary-selection mechanism across the inspected axis families, not as evidence that every insert axis is defective.
Do not infer new public approval or support for uninspected TypeScript syntax.

actions.description: Move the inspected insert-axis starts to the preceding token ends, restricted to horizontal whitespace, and retain comments, optional names, rest parameters and empty-paren behavior.
